summary: A solid Pre-IELTS listening paper: booking guitar lessons, a planetarium director on local radio, two students discussing bias in interviews, and a lecture on the history of chess. All answer keys are correct and in order, and Parts 1–3 have proper IELTS distractors. Parts 1 and 2 are a little short, and most Part 4 notes keep the lecturer's own words, so the paper is somewhat gentler than the real test.
strengths: Part 1 traps work well: electric then acoustic, Tuesday then Wednesday, 7.30 withdrawn then 6.45, 700 corrected to 650, post replaced by text.
Part 2 MCQs reject both wrong options in the script (storm roof and seating; donor; price differences; telescope and tour volunteers).
Part 3 is a genuine academic discussion of research method (leading questions, interviewer effects, neutral venues, anonymity), with three rejected options in each multi-select item.
Answers are concrete single words or numbers within the word limits.

issues.problem: Pair text side 'bought on the website' was not in the script ('bought on the planetarium website').
issues.change: Pair is now ['on the planetarium website', 'online'].

issues.problem: Pair text side 'pushing towards the answer' was not in the script.
issues.change: Pair is now ['leading questions', 'questions that suggested the answer'].

issues.problem: Pair ['set beside', 'compare with'] was not in the script or the option as written.
issues.change: Pair is now ['set our findings beside', 'compare their results with'].

issues.problem: Q7 carried the pair for Q8 (['free of charge', 'included free']).
issues.change: Moved that pair to Q8 ('Included free'), and gave Q7 ['passed his old guitar on to me', 'student has his own guitar'].

issues.problem: The explanation quoted 'not the point', which is not in the script (Madina says 'That's the real cost, not the time').
issues.change: Explanation now says Madina rejects time as the real cost.

issues.problem: Part 4 notes mostly repeat the lecture's wording around the gaps ('the four parts of an {{32}}', 'won by a mathematics teacher from {{38}}', 'the chess {{39}}'), so Part 4 is easier than in the real test.
issues.change: In a future version, paraphrase the notes, e.g. 'named after the four divisions of a {{32}}', 'the winner, a maths teacher, came from {{38}}'.

issues.problem: Script wording problem (Part 4, last paragraph): the lecturer says 'you are reading this sentence in whole words', which does not make sense in a spoken lecture.
issues.change: Report only (audio is recorded). If re-recorded, say 'in the same way that you read a sentence in whole words'.

issues.problem: Parts 1 and 2 are short for IELTS timing (651 and 663 words).
issues.change: If re-recorded, add about 100–150 words to each part, with one more distractor.
